INDEPENDENT REVIEW 3 OF 1.24.40'S PDF TOOLS (the second round of mends) -- 2026-11-25/26
Build under review: the frozen lantern_1240_r3.html (sha256 2d1c4b78ad2268d5...), served as index.html, in Chromium
through Playwright. Line numbers below are of that file. "Old" is the committed 1.24.39 page
(git show lantern-1.24.39:site/index.html, sha256 79891e0b...). I wrote none of the code under review and changed
nothing outside this folder.

How it was tried: 22 PDFs made here (make_fixtures.py), all by programs that are not Lantern --
  reportlab   r_invoice (two pages, header and footer, bullets as code 127, tables at leading 1.0 and 1.15, a Symbol
              ohm) and copies with a CropBox turned 0/90/180/270, linearized with object streams;
  pikepdf     e_textops (one line for each new PDF_TEXT rule: Tm skews, Ts, letters one a Tj at 0.12-0.85 em, single
              letters in 9 pt table cells, WinAnsi 127/129/141/143/144/157, glyph names u1F600 uni20AC, Symbol and
              ZapfDingbats with no /Encoding, a ToUnicode with e+U+0301 and U+FB01/FB03, names broken by hyphens, TeX-like
              a + b = c; page 2: turned runs and forms nested 1 to 10 deep); e_drawing (an A3 drawing: title block in a
              form with a form inside, Symbol units, a ZapfDingbats checklist, dimensions at 90, a 30 degree note, Tz 75)
              and the same sheet stored portrait with /Rotate 90 and a CropBox; f_acro (Acrobat-style: comb fields, radio
              groups drawn with ZapfDingbats l -- plain names, /0 /1 /2 with /Opt export values, UTF-8 names /Gr#C3#BCn
              /Wei#C3#9F -- check boxes with ZapfDingbats 4, /DR /DA), f_orphan (its widgets, no /AcroForm), f_acro_lin,
              f_acro_qflat (flattened by qpdf, as forms are often sent on); h_links (URI, percent-encoded URI, named
              destination, /Contents, a link on a page with no visible name, an outline entry);
  pdflatex    l_manual2 (two columns), l_manual3 (multicol, three columns), l_manual2_t1 (T1 Latin Modern with ToUnicode):
              a pump manual, justified, running heads, footnotes, inline equations, names TeX breaks across lines;
  xelatex     x_intl (DejaVu Serif): Greek with capitals and final sigma, Cyrillic, Turkish dotted/dotless i, micro vs mu,
              increment vs Delta, labels turned 90;
  LibreOffice lo_letter (a flat ODT): header and footer, soft hyphens inside long names, Turkish and Greek names, a table;
  Chromium    c_styles (page.pdf with a header and footer): letter-spacing 0.05-0.9 em, small-caps, a made-up italic,
              sup/sub, tables at line-height 1.0 and 1.15, justified text broken at &shy;, text-transform: uppercase with
              lang=tr and lang=el, a rotate(-90deg) label;
  qpdf        s_deep (a page stamped ten times with --underlay: qpdf wraps stamp and page in a form each time);
  tesseract   t_scan (the invoice as a 150 dpi picture with tesseract's invisible words).
Oracles: poppler (pdftotext, -bbox-layout, pdftoppm -cropbox), qpdf --check and --qdf, pypdf, pdfminer, pikepdf,
pdfplumber (letters of slanted text), tesseract (eng, rus, tur). "Black" means: in the copy's picture, >= 97% of the
box round the original's ink for that word is black (text alone is never that dark, so a word left drawn fails).
  Usage: python3 make_fixtures.py ; python3 run_review.py [new.html] [old.html] [group ...] ; python3 merge.py
  Groups: redact area read fold form tile misc sweep redsweep. Every check is in cases.json (group, file, check,
  expected, got, pass), merged by merge.py from the groups' cases_*.json; a group's .log beside it. Pictures in
  evidence/. About two hours in all, most of it sweep and redsweep (every PDF under tests/fixtures).

COUNTS
@@COUNTS@@

=====================================================================================================================
FAILURES, most serious first  (L = something marked or looked for stays readable; R = regression against 1.24.39;
D = something not marked is lost from the copy; O = over-redaction)
=====================================================================================================================

1. [L] IN TWO- AND THREE-COLUMN TEXT A WORD BROKEN BY A HYPHEN IS NEVER FOUND; BOTH HALVES STAY, AND READERS JOIN THEM
   The round's own claim ("a word broken by a hyphen across two lines of the same column is found and both halves are
   marked") holds only when the page has one column. Lantern's line holds every column at that baseline (pageText
   gathers runs by y alone, 49327), so the "-" that marksOf tests at the end of a line (53009, /([^\s-]+)-$/ on A.low)
   is the rightmost column's, and the word after it (/^(\S+)/ on B.low) is the leftmost column's.
   - l_manual3.pdf (pdflatex, multicol, three columns): redactMarks finds "Winterbourne" 6 times of 12,
     "Featherstonehaugh" 4 of 12; redact() with those marks leaves "Win-"/"terbourne", "Feath-"/"erstonehaugh" drawn
     (evidence/manual3_copy_winterbourne_split.png), and because invisible() keeps both halves (neither holds the
     looked-for word, no mark reaches them) poppler, pypdf and pdfminer read "Winterbourne" in the copy's text (poppler
     takes off the line-end hyphen). The same through the tile: Mark them all says "Marked 6 places", Apply, Save --
     the saved copy shows all six broken ones.
   - l_manual2.pdf and l_manual2_t1.pdf (two columns): 14 of 16 Winterbourne, 15 of 16 Featherstonehaugh, 7 of 8
     Marchetti and Ravenscroft -- every miss is a break in either column (evidence/manual2_copy_split_names.png).
   Smallest reproduction: any two-column page with "Win-" ending a line of the left column and text in the right
   column on that line; redactMarks(boxes, "winterbourne") gives nothing for it.
   Direction: pair runs, not lines -- for a run whose text ends in a hyphen, look on the next baseline down for the run
   that starts within a few points of the same column's left edge (the x where that column's lines start), and join
   those two; keep the one-column case as it is.

2. [L] TURKISH CAPITALS ARE NOT FOUND BY THE NAME AS TYPED; GREEK CAPITALS (WRITTEN WITHOUT ACCENTS) ARE NOT FOUND BY
   THE NAME AS WRITTEN IN RUNNING TEXT
   lc() (52645) keeps a letter whose toLowerCase is longer than one letter as it is, so "İ" stays "İ"; "I" becomes "i";
   "ı" stays "ı". Accents are compared as they are.
   - x_intl.pdf (xelatex): "Şahin" finds nothing of "ŞEBNEM YILDIZ ŞAHİN" (0 of 1); "Yıldız" finds "Yıldız" but not
     "YILDIZ" (1 of 2); "istanbul" finds nothing of "İSTANBUL"; "ışıl" finds nothing of "Işıl". In the copy the
     capitals stay drawn and read (evidence/intl_copy_sahin_yildiz.png: the mixed-case names black, the capitals not).
   - lo_letter.pdf (LibreOffice): "Şahin" 16 of 31 (every "ŞAHİN" missed); c_styles.pdf (Chromium, text-transform:
     uppercase, lang=tr): "Şahin" misses "ŞAHİN".
   - Greek: "Παπαδόπουλος" (typed as it is written in a sentence) finds 1 of 3 -- not "ΠΑΠΑΔΟΠΟΥΛΟΣ" (twice: a heading
     and a turned label); "οδος" finds "ΟΔΟΣ" but not "οδός". Greek capitals are written without accents by rule, so a
     surname typed normally misses every capitalised instance -- the place names and surnames forms put in capitals.
   - The same in the tile: Mark them all "Şahin" -> "Not found"; "Παπαδόπουλος" -> "Marked 1 place".
   Smallest reproduction: redactMarks([{x0:0,x1:100,y:700,size:10,text:"ŞAHİN",parts:[...]}], "şahin") -> [].
   Direction: compare on a folded copy with the length kept letter for letter: İ, I, ı, i all to "i"; Greek letters with
   tonos or dialytika to the bare letter (ά->α, ΐ->ι ...); then 'Şahin' and 'ΠΑΠΑΔΟΠΟΥΛΟΣ' match. For Redact, folding
   more is the safe side.

3. [L] A NAME BROKEN AT ITS OWN HYPHEN IS NEVER FOUND (EVEN IN ONE COLUMN); CHROMIUM'S LINE-BREAK HYPHEN (U+2010) IS NOT
   TAKEN AS ONE
   - e_textops.pdf: "...Ms Philippa Ashworth-" / "Bramley and ...": "Ashworth-Bramley" found 0 times; both halves stay
     drawn (evidence/textops_copy_ashworth_bramley.png). Cause: 53009 /([^\s-]+)-$/ keeps only what follows the last
     earlier hyphen and 53012 joins without the hyphen ("ashworthbramley"), so a phrase with its hyphen never matches.
     Double-barrelled surnames, part numbers (HX-4471-/B) and phone numbers break at their own hyphens all the time.
   - c_styles.pdf (Chromium, &shy;): Chromium breaks with U+2010 ("Featherstone‐" / "haugh", "Win‐" / "terbourne");
     53009 accepts only U+002D, so 3 of 4 Featherstonehaugh and 2 of 3 Winterbourne are found, the broken ones stay
     (evidence/chrome_copy_u2010_breaks.png); same in the tile. LibreOffice's soft-hyphen breaks (U+002D drawn) pass:
     31 of 31.
   - A turned label broken at its hyphen (rotate(-90deg) "Quenby-"/"Ashton"): not found (53010 compares ln.y, which
     means nothing for a turned line).
   Direction: accept [-‐‑­] at the end; try both ta+hb and ta+"-"+hb; take the whole last token
   (/(\S+)[-‐‑­]$/).

4. [R] THE LETTER-SPACING RULE JOINS REAL WORDS: pdfTeX TEXT, SINGLE-CHARACTER TABLE CELLS, EQUATIONS
   49336-49347: the median of the gaps between neighbouring single-letter runs on a line decides; if it lies between
   0.18 and 0.7 of the size, a space is put only where a gap exceeds median + 0.12 em.
   - pdfTeX splits words at kerns into single-letter runs (b|y, F|eatherstonehaugh, d|a|y, curren|t). In justified text
     the gaps between such runs are interword spaces (0.29-0.33 em here), so the median IS the interword gap and words
     fuse. l_manual3.pdf p1: "byFeatherstonehaugh", "aday.", "a+b=c" (poppler and 1.24.39: "by Featherstonehaugh",
     "a day.", "a + b = c"). Runs of one line: b y(-0.28) F(2.91) eatherstonehaugh ... -> gaps between single letters
     [-0.28, 2.91, 109.4] -> median 2.91 pt at 9.96 pt -> no space below 4.1 pt.
   - Single characters in narrow cells (e_textops.pdf, 9-9.5 pt pitch at 9 pt, as a connector's pin row, a keypad,
     a seat map): "Keys: 1234567890" and "Pins: ABCDEFGHJ K" (poppler and 1.24.39: "1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9 0", "A B C D ...").
     Ten digits read as one ten-digit number is a change of meaning.
   - Equations: "a + b = c" with TeX's medium and thick spaces -> "a+b=c" (l_manual2/3 and e_textops).
   - Not only TeX's kerns: xelatex (xdvipdfmx) writes each word as its own run, so any line with a few one-letter
     words or symbols fuses them. Review 2's own pdf_review2_1240/x_nonlatin.pdf p1, which 1.24.39 read exactly as
     poppler does: "Symbols: R = 4.7 kΩ, U ≤ 230 V, I ≥ 2 A, ±0.5 %, 25 µm, √2, x → y, ∑ = 12." is now
     "Symbols: R= 4.7 kΩ, U≤ 230 V,I≥2 A, ±0.5 %, 25 µm, √2, x→y,∑= 12." (words against poppler 1.000 -> 0.876).
     A search for "≥ 2 A" or "U ≤ 230" now fails there.
   - Consequences: Text Reader, Chat and copy get fused words; a phrase search ("by Featherstonehaugh", "a day")
     fails; and Redact's whole-word extension then blacks the fused neighbour: in the redacted l_manual3 copy "by" is
     black (100% of its letters) before Featherstonehaugh.
   Words against poppler fall on l_manual2 (F1 0.930 -> 0.916), l_manual2_t1, l_manual3 (0.896 -> 0.879).
   Direction: apply the rule only to a sequence of at least 3-4 consecutive single-letter runs with nearly equal gaps
   (max - min below ~0.06 em, as CSS letter-spacing gives exactly), each run one letter of the same font and size;
   pdfTeX's kerned splits (gaps that alternate between ~0 and an interword space) and table cells (a multi-letter
   header beside them, gaps equal to a column pitch) then keep the old rule. Gather the gaps per column, not per line.

5. [D, L] FORMS NESTED MORE THAN 8 DEEP: NEITHER DRAWN NOR READ, AND REDACT SILENTLY DROPS THEM FROM THE COPY
   PDF_TEXT (49268) and PDF_DRAW (50119) stop at depth 8; poppler draws all ten.
   - s_deep.pdf: the invoice-like base page stamped ten times by qpdf --underlay (qpdf wraps the stamp and the old page
     in a form each time: after ten stamps the original page is 10 deep). Lantern shows a page with stamps 3-10 only:
     "Base page: Lindale Penrith Ulverston", "Stamp 1: Ambleside", "Stamp 2: Bowness" are not drawn and not found.
     Redact of anything on that page produces a copy without them (evidence/deep_original.png vs
     deep_copy_base_page_gone.png): the document's own content is gone and nothing says so. e_textops.pdf p2 (hand-made,
     10 deep): "Depth 9 Ireby", "Depth 10 Keswick" lost from the redacted copy the same way.
   - Not a regression (1.24.39 read 3 deep and drew 8), but this round raised reading to 8 to match drawing; a page that
     has been through nine stamping tools is still blank where its text was.
   Direction: follow forms as deep as they go with a guard against cycles (the set of form objects on the current
   path) and an operation budget, in both modules; if a limit is ever hit, Redact should refuse ("this page has parts
   Lantern cannot draw") rather than burn a picture that lacks them.

6. [L, low] LINKS: A PERCENT-ENCODED ADDRESS IS KEPT; A LINK ON A PAGE WITH NO MARK KEEPS THE NAME; NAMED DESTINATIONS
   h_links.pdf, redact "Okonkwo" (found on page 1):
   - page 1 keeps the link "https://records.example.org/scan?name=%4Fkonkwo%20T": 52825-52826 lowercase the address
     first and decode it after, so %4F decodes to a capital "O" and "Okonkwo t" does not contain "okonkwo". Decode,
     then lowercase.
   - page 2 (no visible name, nothing marked) keeps "https://pacs.example.org/folder/OKONKWO_T/" -- links are only
     looked at on marked pages (52809). The named destination "Okonkwo_record" (/Names /Dests, kept by keepCatalog)
     and the outline title stay as well; Apply's message names bookmarks, not links on other pages or destination
     names. Direction: look at every page's links (and /Dests names) for the words looked for, or say so in Apply's
     message.

7. [O] THROUGH THE API, A FORM FIELD'S VALUE IS MARKED BY AN ESTIMATE THAT RUNS PAST IT AND BLACKS ITS NEIGHBOURS
   pageText places a field's value from 0.6 em a letter (49302: 1.1 * max(0.6 * sz * len, Helvetica width)), so
   "Gwendolyn Featherstonehaugh" (11 pt) is spread over 196 pt where it is drawn over 153 pt. redactMarks then puts
   "Featherstonehaugh" at 274-399 (drawn at 260-355) and "Wharfedale" at 274-341 (drawn at 247-298). redact() flattens,
   finds the words again where they are drawn (52796-52800) and ADDS those marks, but keeps the estimated ones: in
   f_acro, f_orphan and f_acro_lin copies "Rise," and "Otley" (the next words of the address) are black and gone from
   the copy's words (evidence/acro_copy_neighbours_blacked.png). Nothing leaks; the tile is not affected (it flattens
   before marking). Direction: in redact(), when the PDF was flattened and the words were found again, drop the marks
   that came from the unflattened page's field and comment parts (parts with no q); and estimate with Helvetica's
   widths only (no 0.6 em floor).

8. [L, low] A NAME WRITTEN WITH A COMBINING ACCENT, OR WITH A LIGATURE CODE POINT, IS NOT FOUND
   e_textops.pdf: the PDF's ToUnicode maps é to e+U+0301 and ffi/fi to U+FB03/U+FB01 (as some Mac and InDesign PDFs
   do). "José" finds nothing of "José" (decomposed), "Griffiths" nothing of "Griﬃths", "Clifford" nothing of
   "Cliﬁord"; all stay drawn and in every reader's text (evidence/textops_copy_jose_griffiths.png).
   Direction: compare NFKC-normalised text (String.prototype.normalize, feature-detected) with an index map back to the
   letters, or at least map U+FB00-FB06 and strip U+0300-036F on both sides.
   Related drift (not a leak): for a standard font named without /Widths, PDF_TEXT (49155) and PDF_DRAW (50004)
   measure a code by its ToUnicode text, so a code mapped to "e"+U+0301 is two letters wide; on that line the words
   after José sit 5.6 pt further right per such letter than in poppler (17 pt by "of"), in the viewer and in a redacted
   copy's picture. Measure the glyph (its code's standard width), not its Unicode text.

9. [L, low] LIMITS OF THE NEW READING THAT LEAVE WORDS UNFINDABLE
   - Letter-spacing of 0.7 em or more (c_styles.pdf "TOP AINSWORTH" at 0.7 em, "WIDE BOOTHROYD" at 0.9 em): read
     "A I N S W O R T H", so "Ainsworth" is not found and stays (as the rule says: median < 0.7).
   - A comb field already flattened by another program (f_acro_qflat.pdf, digits one a 20 pt cell, 1.1 em apart):
     "078051120" and "9185550143" are read as separate digits and cannot be found; Redact leaves them. Poppler reads
     them as separate digits too, so this is a limit, not a regression; the drag-over mark works. Worth a word in the
     "Not found" message ("letters spaced apart, as in a comb box, are not found: drag over them").

10. [D, low] REDACT NOW FLATTENS EVERY PAGE'S FIELDS; A FORM WITH NO DRAWINGS OF ITS OWN COMES OUT LOOKING DIFFERENT
   needsFlat (52771-52779) flattens all widgets whenever any page has one (this round's mend for item 2 of review 2).
   Where the form carries no appearance streams (NeedAppearances true, as pypdf and many scripts write), flatten's
   plain() (52227-52233) draws each field itself, and the redacted copy -- every page of it, marked or not -- no longer
   looks as other viewers showed it. pdf_review1_1239/form_hand.pdf, redact "Hopper": the list box "Wrench / Hammer /
   Screwdriver" becomes the line "Wrench, Screwdriver" (Hammer gone), the comb "7 4 0 7 0" becomes "74070" outside its
   cells, the ticks become drawn paths (no longer text). pdf_review2_1239/strings.pdf: values with letters outside
   WinAnsi drawn as "?" ("U16: Ohm ü ?? ??"). Also pdf_review2_1239/forms2.pdf, form_pypdf_filled_regen.pdf (the
   redsweep group's "lost" rows). Nothing marked leaks; what was not marked changes. Direction: draw a list box's
   options and a comb's cells in plain() (fillForm's textAP already draws combs), or flatten only the marked pages'
   fields and drop the others' widgets after copying their values into the text layer.

11. [O, minor] SLANTED (30 DEGREE) WORDS: ONE BOX A LETTER, AS CLAIMED, BUT THE FIRST BOX TAKES THE NEIGHBOUR'S EDGE
   e_drawing.pdf "SEE DETAIL A, Ravensworth" at 30 degrees: the boxes cover Ravensworth completely (checked by eye,
   evidence/drawing_copy_30deg_ravensworth.png), and its first box covers the comma and touches the "A" before it, so
   "A," leaves the copy's words. Inherent in upright rectangles; known from review 2 (its item 15).

@@SWEEP@@

=====================================================================================================================
CHECKS THAT FAILED BECAUSE THE ORACLE WAS WRONG, OR MY FIXTURE (said plainly)
=====================================================================================================================
 - Slanted text: poppler cuts 30-degree words into fragments ("G", "oa", "th", "lan" for Goathland), on the
   original and differently on the copy. The "mark lies over a word looked for", "cut" and "lost" checks of
   e_drawing / e_drawing_rot90 / textops_p2 near Ravensworth and Goathland count those fragments; the marks are where
   the words are (pdfplumber's letters, and by eye).
 - pypdf ignores Tz when it places letters: Lantern writes each kept letter with Tz fitting Helvetica to the
   original letter's width, so where the original font is wider (DejaVu, Liberation Serif) pypdf splits the copy's
   words ("Sor umlu", "Н овосибирск"); a two-line PDF made here shows the same ("Sorumlu" with r at Tz 150 ->
   pypdf "Sor umlu", poppler "Sorumlu"). The letters are all there; pypdf-based pipelines will see split words.
 - e_textops.pdf's glyph-name line (u1F600 ... on a non-embedded Helvetica): poppler gives those names no width, so its
   words there sit elsewhere; my fixture is unusual, and that line is left out of the "words kept" check.
 - poppler reads Chromium's letter-spaced capitals as single letters ("P R I VAT E C A L D E R B A N K"); Lantern's
   joined reading is right there. Poppler also reads the comb digits one by one (item 9).
 - poppler loops for ever on review 2's pdf_review2_1239/ve_cycle.pdf, writing output without end (it ran my sweep
   out of memory once); both sweeps leave that one file out.
 - pdf_review1_1240/t_inherit.pdf (redsweep "lost 3 of 4"): its line is drawn with its baseline on the page's top edge,
   so its letters lie outside the page as seen; poppler reads them, the copy leaves them out by the round's own rule
   (a letter is kept when its start or middle is on the page). Not a fault.
 - stamped10 (Lantern's Stamp ten times, then Redact): my stamps were drawn over the invoice's own header, 7 pt apart
   at 8 pt; the "cut" row there counts words lying under the stamped words, which any mark over them must cover.
 - The field-value rows of item 7 ("not grossly bigger") are real; the "lies over a word looked for" rows of
   acro_filled are the same estimate.
 - My own harness mistakes, mended before the rows in cases.json: pdftoppm without -cropbox (pictures of cropped
   pages misaligned); P.pdfDocBytes taken for a file's bytes (it encodes text); a stamp of mine drawn over the
   invoice's "Reservoir"; UTF-8 radio names written twice-encoded by pikepdf; a second tool bar's Apply clicked. The
   rows of the cases re-run after each (cases_redact_rerun*.json) replace the first run's in cases.json.

=====================================================================================================================
WHAT PASSED
=====================================================================================================================
PDF_TEXT, the round's rules (each against poppler and 1.24.39):
 - A Tm skew of 0.25, 0.5 and -0.3 stays in its line ("Level start Penhaligon ends here."; 1.24.39 glued it:
   "Level startPenhaligonends"); Chromium's made-up italic stays in its line; a slanted 20 pt title reads whole.
 - A word raised by Ts 6 and one lowered by Ts -3 stay in their line, and their marks are where they are drawn.
 - Letters one a Tj at 0.12, 0.25, 0.45, 0.65 em, and Chromium's letter-spacing at 0.05-0.5 em, read as words with
   the spaces in the right places ("PRIVATE FILE WOLSTENHOLME", "Engineer Wolstenholme signs (0.3em)"; 1.24.39:
   "E n g i n e e r ..."); found and redacted (Wolstenholme, Hargreaves, Calderbank, Meriweather).
 - Forms 8 deep are read (e_textops "Depth 8 Hawkshead", s_deep "Stamp 3: Coniston").
 - Symbol and ZapfDingbats with no /Encoding: "R1 = 4.7 kΩ ±5%, α = 30°, ∆p ≤ 2 bar, µ = 0.15, d ≥ 12" and
   "✔ ✓ ✘ ■ ❑" read as poppler reads them (the ohm as U+2126), drawn with about poppler's ink and nearer poppler's
   picture than 1.24.39 (which drew "W a D £ m ³" and "4 3 8 n q"); marks after a Symbol letter start where poppler's
   words do. ZapfDingbats 0xAC (①) is read as nothing, as the round says (poppler: ①).
 - WinAnsi 127, 129, 141, 143, 144, 157 read as bullets ("Tulsa • Tel • 918 ..."), the words after them in place.
 - Glyph names u1F600, uni20AC, u2126, Omega, uni00E9, u1F4A1 read as 😀 € Ω Ω é 💡.
 - Parts in boxes carry y and size (a field's value, a typed comment); a typed comment's word is marked where its
   drawing puts it (Hollingworth: mark 364.7-435.4, poppler 369.7-435.7, on its line).
Redact (find, then Apply; and drag-over areas):
 - Gone from poppler's, pypdf's and pdfminer's text, the unpacked bytes (as text, UTF-16 and as the letters shown in
   order), the picture and tesseract's reading: the invoice's names, a hyphenated surname, phone numbers inside
   longer ones, at leading 1.0 and 1.15, with a CropBox turned 0/90/180/270, linearized with object streams; a skewed,
   a raised, a lowered, a Tz 150 and a Tc 3 word; turned 90/270/180 words and a 30 degree word (one box a letter);
   a title block in nested forms; Symbol-unit lines; xelatex Greek and Cyrillic (level and turned 90, final sigma
   capitals); LibreOffice soft-hyphen breaks (31 of 31); Chromium letter-spaced names; tesseract's scan; an invoice
   stamped ten times by Lantern's own Stamp.
 - Forms: an Acrobat-style form, the same with object streams and linearized, and a page with widgets and no
   /AcroForm: every field flattened, the comb SSN and phone covered whole (the field box) through the API and the
   tile; a form filled by fillForm then redacted.
 - Words not looked for: on every case without a cause above, every word away from the marks is found again by
   poppler, in its place; at leading 1.0 (9 pt rows) no neighbour loses more than a sliver (no word over 15%).
 - Kept Greek and Cyrillic letters come back from pypdf too (the extra fonts' ToUnicode works; spaces aside).
Fill in and forms:
 - P.fields lists each radio group's choices by export value ([Day, Night, Swing], [Klein, Mittel, Große], [Grün,
   Weiß, Blau] for UTF-8 names) and its value; fillForm sets a group by state name, by /Opt value (Große -> /2) or by
   its UTF-8 name (Grün -> /Gr#C3#BCn), leaves it for a value none has, turns all off for ""; pypdf and poppler agree
   (the dot drawn in the chosen button only). The tile shows the nine buttons as radios, writes Night, Große and Grün,
   and shows them chosen when opened again. A Greek value typed in a field reads back as typed (/ActualText).
 - A stamp comment with Cyrillic, Ω and ≤ carries /ActualText (poppler reads "ПРИВЕТ KΩ ≤ 5 OK"), and the tools'
   note names the letters drawn as "?".
 - Turned from 844 x 390 to 390 x 844 the page refits (no sideways scroll) and back again; after the person zooms in,
   turning keeps their zoom.
